24581-colonel-john-brown-of-pittsfield-m.title: Colonel John Brown Of Pittsfield Massachusetts The Brave Acc
24581-colonel-john-brown-of-pittsfield-m.creator: Unknown
24581-colonel-john-brown-of-pittsfield-m.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Daniel Brown, the father of Colonel John Brown, came from Haverhill, Mass., to the western part of the Commonwealth in 1752, when his son John was eight years old. He seems to have been first in the beautiful town of Sandisfield to take part in its local government, both secular and ecclesiastical.

arxiv-1809-09518.title: On root-ratio multipoint methods for finding multiple zeros of univariate functions
arxiv-1809-09518.creator: Miodrag S. Petković, Ljiljana D. Petković, [2mm] Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš[-1mm] A. Medvedeva 14, 18000 Niš, Serbia
arxiv-1809-09518.description: Abstract Several root-ratio multipoint methods for finding multiple zeros of univariate functions were recently presented. The characteristic of these methods is that they deal with m m -th root of ratio of two functions (hence the name root-ratio methods), where m m is the multiplicity of the sought zero, known in advance.

arxiv-2112-00401.title: Stochastic integration with respect to local time of the Brownian sheet and regularising properties of Brownian sheet paths Thanks: The project on which this publication is based has been carried out with funding provided by the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, under the programme financed by the
arxiv-2112-00401.creator: Antoine-Marie Bogso, Moustapha Dieye, Olivier Menoukeu Pamen
arxiv-2112-00401.description: Abstract . In this work, we generalise the stochastic local time space integration introduced in [ 11 ] to the case of Brownian sheet. This allows us to prove a generalised two-parameter Itô formula and derive Davie type inequalities for the Brownian sheet. Such estimates are useful to obtain regularity bounds for some averaging type operators along Brownian sheet curves.

arxiv-2302-02961.title: Double excitations in the AdS(5)/CFT(4)
arxiv-2302-02961.creator: integrable system
arxiv-2302-02961.description: Abstract HU-EP-23/05 Abstract: It is argued that the integrable model for the planar spectrum of the AdS/CFT correspondence can accommodate for the full spectrum of excitations D^{\alpha\dot{\alpha}},\phi^{[IJ]},\psi^{I},\bar{\psi}_{I},F^{\alpha\beta},\tilde{F}^{\dot{\alpha}\dot{\beta}} (with I,J\in 1\ldots 4 ) if double excitations are allowed for all three raising operators of the internal SU(4) symmetry.

arxiv-2303-16125.title: Mapping quantum algorithms to multi-core quantum computing architectures
arxiv-2303-16125.creator: Anabel Ovide 1 , Santiago Rodrigo 2 , Medina Bandic 3 , Hans Van Someren 3 , Sebastian Feld 3 , Sergi Abadal 2 , Eduard Alarcon 2 , and Carmen G. Almudever 1
arxiv-2303-16125.description: Abstract Current monolithic quantum computer architectures have limited scalability. One promising approach for scaling them up is to use a modular or multi-core architecture, in which different quantum processors (cores) are connected via quantum and classical links. This new architectural design poses new challenges such as the expensive inter-core communication.

arxiv-2304-10753.title: Hunting scalar partners of the Higgs boson at the LHC
arxiv-2304-10753.description: Abstract Composite Higgs models with a fermionic ultraviolet completion predict in general additional pseudo Nambu Goldstone bosons beside the Higgs multiplet. In this contribution we discuss their LHC signatures and present first bounds in simplified models which can also be applied to generic models like multi-Higgs models.

arxiv-2310-14729.title: MAS: Multi-view Ancestral Sampling for 3D Motion Generation Using 2D Diffusion
arxiv-2310-14729.creator: Roy Kapon, Guy Tevet, Daniel Cohen-Or, Amit H. Bermano
arxiv-2310-14729.description: Abstract We introduce Multi-view Ancestral Sampling (MAS), a method for 3D motion generation, using 2D diffusion models that were trained on motions obtained from in-the-wild videos. As such, MAS opens opportunities to exciting and diverse fields of motion previously under-explored as 3D data is scarce and hard to collect.

arxiv-2402-13339.title: Criticality in the Luria-Delbrück model with an arbitrary mutation rate
arxiv-2402-13339.creator: Deng Pan, Jie Lin, Ariel Amir
arxiv-2402-13339.description: Abstract The Luria-Delbrück model is a classic model of population dynamics with random mutations, that has been used historically to prove that random mutations drive evolution. In typical scenarios, the relevant mutation rate is exceedingly small, and mutants are counted only at the final time point.

arxiv-2403-16683.title: Optimal Mass Transport of Nonlinear Systems under Input and Density Constraints
arxiv-2403-16683.creator: Dongjun Wu, Anders Rantzer
arxiv-2403-16683.description: Abstract We investigate optimal mass transport problem of affine-nonlinear dynamical systems with input and density constraints. Three algorithms are proposed to tackle this problem, including two Uzawa-type methods and a splitting algorithm based on the Douglas-Rachford algorithm. Some preliminary simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approaches.

arxiv-2406-08692.title: The cancellation property for projective modules over integral group rings
arxiv-2406-08692.creator: John Nicholson
arxiv-2406-08692.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by John Nicholson. We obtain a partial classification of the finite groups G G for which the integral group ring ℤ ​ G \mathbb{Z}G has projective cancellation, i.e. for which P ⊕ ℤ ​ G ≅ Q ⊕ ℤ ​ G P\oplus\mathbb{Z}G\cong Q\oplus\mathbb{Z}G implies P ≅ Q P\cong Q for projective ℤ ​ G \mathbb{Z}G -modules P P and Q Q . In particular, we determine when projective cancellation holds for a finite group with no exceptional binary polyhedral quotients.

arxiv-2410-05751.title: Asymptotic Equivalence of Locally Stationary Processes and Bivariate Gaussian White Noise
arxiv-2410-05751.creator: Cristina Butucea, Alexander Meister, Angelika Rohde
arxiv-2410-05751.description: Abstract We consider a general class of statistical experiments, in which an n n -dimensional centered Gaussian random variable is observed and its covariance matrix is the parameter of interest. The covariance matrix is assumed to be well-approximable in a linear space of lower dimension K n K_{n} with eigenvalues uniformly bounded away from zero and infinity.

arxiv-2411-02931.title: A resolved, multi-wavelength study of gas-rich dwarf galaxies in the Fornax cluster using MUSE, MeerKAT, and ALMA
arxiv-2411-02931.creator: Nikki Zabel, Alessandro Loni, Marc Sarzi, Paolo Serra, Arjun Chawla, Timothy A. Davis, Dane Kleiner, S. Ilani Loubser, Reynier Peletier
arxiv-2411-02931.description: Abstract We combine new and archival MUSE observations with data from the MeerKAT Fornax Survey and the ALMA Fornax Cluster Survey to study the ionised, atomic, and molecular gas in six gas-rich dwarf galaxies in the Fornax cluster in detail.

arxiv-2502-06479.title: On invex functions with same η \eta in single- and multivalued nonsmooth optimization with Clarke’s subdifferential
arxiv-2502-06479.creator: Ville Rinne, Yury Nikulin, Marko M. Mäkelä
arxiv-2502-06479.description: Abstract In this paper, a finite family of nonsmooth locally Lipschitz continuous functions that are invex with respect to the same function η \eta are characterized in terms of their scalarized counterparts. Keywords: Invexity, nonsmooth analysis, Clarke’s subdifferential, single- and multivalued optimization. MSC2020: 90C56, 49J52.

arxiv-2505-22342.title: Progressive Data Dropout: An Embarrassingly Simple Approach to Train Faster
arxiv-2505-22342.creator: Shriram M S, Xinyue Hao, Shihao Hou, Yang Lu, Laura Sevilla-Lara, Anurag Arnab, Shreyank N Gowda
arxiv-2505-22342.description: Abstract The success of the machine learning field has reliably depended on training on large datasets. While effective, this trend comes at an extraordinary cost. This is due to two deeply intertwined factors: the size of models and the size of datasets.

arxiv-2601-07339.title: Impact of Boundary Conditions on the Double-Kicked Quantum Rotor
arxiv-2601-07339.creator: Victoria Motsch, Nikolai Bolik, Sandro Wimberger
arxiv-2601-07339.description: Abstract We study the on-resonance Spin-1/2 Double Kicked Rotor, a periodically driven quantum system that hosts topological phases. Motivated by experimental constraints, we analyze the effects of open and periodic boundary conditions in contrast to the idealized case of infinite momentum space.

arxiv-2601-21847.title: READY: Reward Discovery for Meta-Black-Box Optimization
arxiv-2601-21847.creator: Zechuan Huang, Zhiguang Cao, Hongshu Guo, Yue-Jiao Gong, Zeyuan Ma
arxiv-2601-21847.description: Abstract Meta-Black-Box Optimization (MetaBBO) is an emerging avenue within Optimization community, where algorithm design policy could be meta-learned by reinforcement learning to enhance optimization performance. So far, the reward functions in existing MetaBBO works are designed by human experts, introducing certain design bias and risks of reward hacking.

arxiv-2602-11245.title: Stratified Sampling for Quasi-Probability Decompositions
arxiv-2602-11245.creator: Joshua W. Dai, Bálint Koczor
arxiv-2602-11245.description: Abstract Quasi-probability decompositions (QPDs) have proven essential in many quantum algorithms and protocols—one replaces a “difficult” quantum circuit with an ensemble of “easier” circuit variants whose weighted outcomes reproduce any target observable. This, however, inevitably yields an increased configuration variance beyond Born-rule shot noise.

arxiv-2606-00940.title: Programmable site-selective spin control in rotating Penning-trap ion crystals
arxiv-2606-00940.creator: Nihar Makadia, Julian Y. Z. Jee, Gustavo Café de Miranda, Joseph H. Pham, Michael J. Biercuk, Athreya Shankar, Robert N. Wolf

pmc-10536793.title: B-Cell Lymphoma of the Middle Ear Treated with Multidrug Chemotherapy in a Cat
pmc-10536793.creator: Tomoko Takahashi, Hiroyuki Nagata, Hirotaka Kondo
pmc-10536793.description: Simple SummaryFeline lymphoma can arise in a variety of sites, with the pathogenesis differing according to the site of origin. Although cases of primary lymphoma of the middle ear have been reported, information on treatment efficacy and prognosis remains lacking. In this study, an 11-year-old, spayed female mixed-breed cat was diagnosed with primary lymphoma of the middle ear.

pmc-11406709.title: Access and barriers to safer supply prescribing during a toxic drug emergency: a mixed methods study of implementation in British Columbia, Canada
pmc-11406709.creator: Karen A Urbanoski, Thea van Roode, Marion Selfridge, Katherine C Hogan, James Fraser, Kurt Lock, Phoenix Beck McGreevy, Charlene Burmeister, Brittany Barker, Amanda Slaunwhite, Bohdan Nosyk, Bernadette Pauly
pmc-11406709.description: BackgroundIn March 2020, British Columbia, Canada, introduced prescribed safer supply involving the distribution of pharmaceutical grade alternatives to the unregulated toxic drug supply. Prior research has demonstrated positive impacts on overdose mortality, but with limited reach to people who use substances.

pmc-11430263.title: Development and external validation of clinical predictive model for stress urinary incontinence in Chinese women : a multicenter retrospective study
pmc-11430263.creator: Dan Zhang, Min Zhou, Mingya Zhang, Youfang Zhang, Donghui Wu, Ruijuan Weng, Min Tang, Zvikomborero Panashe Rejoice Munemo, Hongxiu Zhang
pmc-11430263.description: BackgroundStress urinary incontinence (SUI), the prevalent form of urinary incontinence, significantly impairs women’s quality of life. This study aims to create a visual nomogram to estimate the risk of SUI within one year postpartum for early intervention in high-risk Chinese women.MethodsWe recruited 1,531 postpartum women who gave birth at two hospitals in Kunshan City from 2021 to 2022.

pmc-11455947.title: Use of physiologically based kinetic modeling to predict neurotoxicity and genotoxicity of methylglyoxal in humans
pmc-11455947.creator: Liang Zheng, Xiyu Li, Frances Widjaja, Chen Liu, Ivonne M. C. M. Rietjens
pmc-11455947.description: This study aimed to evaluate human neurotoxicity and genotoxicity risks from dietary and endogenous methylglyoxal (MGO), utilizing physiologically based kinetic (PBK) modeling-facilitated reverse dosimetry as a new approach methodology (NAM) to extrapolate in vitro toxicity data to in vivo dose-response predictions.

pmc-11514024.title: Effect of Internal and Bulge Loops on the Thermal Stability of Small DNA Duplexes
pmc-11514024.creator: Earle Stellwagen, Paul J. Barnard, Nancy C. Stellwagen
pmc-11514024.description: The thermal stabilities of DNA duplexes analogous to the let-7 microRNA:lin-41 mRNA complex from Caenorhabditis elegans have been measured by free solution capillary electrophoresis. DNA duplexes with the same stems but different types of internal or bulge loops and a control with no loop have also been studied.

pmc-11611776.title: CX3CR1 + CD8 + T cells: Key players in antitumor immunity
pmc-11611776.creator: Jiajin Ma, Yue Wu, Shaoxian Wu, Zhang Fang, Lujun Chen, Jingting Jiang, Xiao Zheng
pmc-11611776.description: CX3CR1 functions as the specific receptor for the chemokine CX3CL1, demonstrating expression across a broad spectrum of immune cells. This underscores its pivotal role in communication and response mechanisms within the immune system. Upon engagement with CX3CL1, CX3CR1 initiates a cascade of downstream signaling pathways that regulate various biological functions.

pmc-11963949.title: Portrayal of Acute Myocardial Infarction in Popular Film: A Review of Gender, Race, and Ethnicity
pmc-11963949.creator: Kirsten E. Shaw, Kevin M. Harris, Amy Diedrich, Amy K. Holbrook, Larissa Stanberry, Michelle D. Carlson, Retu Saxena
pmc-11963949.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). from ethnic and racial minority groups have been largely unsuccessful, with recent national surveys showing a significant decline in public awareness that CVD is the leading cause of death in women. 2 Given the increasing influence of popular media narratives on public health, we sought to investigate how acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is depicted in popular film to understand the representation of women, diverse populations, and symptoms.

pmc-12432921.title: Tumor necrosis, an independent prognostic factor for predicting gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors
pmc-12432921.creator: Kunlong Chang, Renjie Li, Peng Zhang, Tao Chen, Haibo Qiu, Yongjian Zhou, Chunyan Du, Xiaonan Yin, Fang Pan, Guoliang Zheng, Yan Zhao, Xiufeng Liu, Jian Li, Bo Zhang, Ye Zhou, Jiang Yu, Kaixiong Tao, Yong Li, Xingyu Feng
pmc-12432921.description: BackgroundTumor necrosis has been identified as an independent adverse prognostic factor in various human malignancies; however, its prognostic value in gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors (gGISTs) remains uncertain. This study aimed to investigate the association between tumor necrosis and overall survival (OS) in patients with gGIST who underwent radical surgical resection.

pmc-12700868.title: An integration of deep learning models for effective classification of human activity patterns in disabled people using gesture analysis
pmc-12700868.creator: Hend Khalid Alkahtani, Nouf Al-Kahtani, Gouse Pasha Mohammed, Radwa Marzouk
pmc-12700868.description: Human activity recognition (HAR) has numerous applications due to its widespread use of procurement tools, such as smartphones and video cameras, and its ability to capture data on human activity. HAR became a hot scientific area in the computer vision (CV) domain.

pmc-12933752.title: Identifying innovative models of urgent care in rural coastal areas in England: the Elevate study - a mixed-methods protocol
pmc-12933752.creator: Pete Lampard, Joy Adamson, Helen Anderson, Lisa Ballantine, Fiona Bell, Jonathan Richard Benger, Rebecca Louise Blakey, Phillip Dickinson, Steven Dykes, James Gaughan, Stuart Maitland-Knibb, Daniel Mensah, Zacharia Alice Ransome, Gerry Richardson, Rita Santos, Rebecca Sheridan, Peter Sivey, Ed Smith
pmc-12933752.description: AbstractIntroductionUrgent and emergency care (UEC) systems in England face unprecedented pressures, with record accident and emergency attendances, persistent breaches of ambulance response targets and poorer outcomes for time-sensitive conditions. National UEC recovery plans have introduced multiple innovations—such as same-day emergency care, virtual wards and specialty hubs—to manage these pressures and improve patient flow.

pmc-12966985.title: The role of GH/IGF-1 axis dysfunction and inflammatory cytokines in pediatric short stature
pmc-12966985.creator: Qingfu Yang, Shanshan Chen, Tieniu Wu, Jingxin Peng, Lidan Mao
pmc-12966985.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundShort stature in children is a common clinical condition frequently associated with abnormalities in the GH/IGF-1 axis. Emerging evidence points to the involvement of inflammatory cytokines and serum markers in modulating this dysfunction. This study aims to investigate the molecular pathways underlying GH/IGF-1 axis impairment and assess the levels of inflammatory cytokines and other related biomarkers in children with short stature.MethodsA total of 150 children diagnosed with short stature were recruited from the endocrinology department of a tertiary care hospital.

pmc-13233525.title: Adverse neurological events associated with bispecific T cell engagers in oncology: a real-world study
pmc-13233525.creator: Qianqian Cui, Shuangqi Gao, Hongyu Liu, Haiyun Zhou, Yunxiao Li
pmc-13233525.description: BackgroundWith the increasing use of bispecific T cell engagers (BiTEs) in anti-tumor immunotherapy, the associated adverse reactions pose significant challenges to clinical application. Nervous system toxicity (NST) is one of the notable adverse events associated with this class of drugs. This study aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of BiTE-induced nervous system adverse events.

pmc-13268873.title: Risk prediction models for postoperative atrial fibrillation in patients with lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13268873.creator: Fei Yang, Tenglu Sun, Yi Shang, Yuanyuan Chen, Jinxiang Wu, Xuli Shang
pmc-13268873.description: BackgroundPostoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a common and clinically significant complication following lung cancer surgery, associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Although numerous prediction models have been developed to estimate POAF risk, their overall performance and methodological quality remain unclear.

pmc-13407205.title: 婴儿脓肿分枝杆菌肺病1例并文献复习
pmc-13407205.creator: 秋艳 金, 志翔 伍, 作成 杨, 卓颖 李
pmc-13407205.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 脓肿分枝杆菌引起的肺部感染在无基础肺部疾病的儿童中是罕见的，尤其是在婴儿中。中南大学湘雅三医院于2023年7月29日收治1例3月龄女婴，该女婴以咳嗽为唯一表现，肺部CT显示双肺多发片状、团块状高密度影，送检肺泡灌洗液行宏基因组测序，确诊为脓肿分枝杆菌肺病，进一步免疫缺陷评估及全外显子组测序均无异常，予阿米卡星、头孢西丁、利奈唑胺和阿奇霉素联合治疗后病情好转，未见不良反应。对于临床表现不典型且常规病原学检测阳性率低的婴儿肺部感染(尤其是罕见病原体所致)，宏基因组测序有助于早期诊断。 脓肿分枝杆菌(Mycobacterium abscessus)肺部感染通常发生在有潜在危险因素的患者中，包括囊性纤维化(cystic fibrosis，CF)、慢性肺病和免疫功能低下状态[1]，主要病变是气管内病变和肺门淋巴结肿大[2]，很少发生在无潜在危险因素的儿童中，尤其是小婴儿[3]。鉴于目前缺乏具有既定疗效、安全性的标准化治疗方案和最佳治疗时间，笔者报告1例无免疫缺陷的婴儿脓肿分枝杆菌肺病，经阿米卡星、头孢西丁、利奈唑胺和阿奇霉素联合等治疗，成功地控制了病情，且未出现不良反应。 病例资料 患儿，女，3个月，因咳嗽9 d于2023年7月29日收入中南大学湘雅三医院(以下简称“我院”)儿科。患儿入院前9 d无明显诱因出现咳嗽，为单声咳，吐白色泡沫样痰，无发热，无喘息、气促等症状。患儿系31+4周早产儿，已接种卡介苗。入院体格检查：体温为37 ℃，脉搏为166次/min，呼吸为44次/min；体重为3.5 kg，身长为52 cm，均低于同年龄、同性别正常儿童生长曲线的第3百分位；经皮血氧饱和度为95%。精神反应可，全身浅表淋巴结未触及，卡疤无红肿、破溃。咽部无充血，无鼻翼煽动。胸廓双侧肋缘外翻，可见三凹征，双肺呼吸音粗，可闻及哮鸣音及湿啰音。心脏体格检查无异常。肝右肋下2 cm，质中，脾脏未触及。血常规示：血红蛋白为116 g/L，白细胞计数为9.8×109/L，中性粒细胞比值为0.406，血小板计数为306×109/L。C反应蛋白<5 mg/L，降钙素原为0.06 ng/mL。血生化检查未见异常，血结核杆菌抗体免疫球蛋白(immunoglobulin，Ig)G、IgM均为阴性。胸片示双肺野可见片状高密度影，边界欠清晰(图1A)，考虑双肺感染。入院后予以头孢他啶抗感染，第2天行纤维支气管镜下肺泡灌洗术，术中各段支气管管腔内可见较多白色絮状分泌物，以中下叶为甚。术后取肺泡灌洗液(bronchoalveolar lavage fluid，BALF)标本送检，2 d后结果回报：BALF宏基因组测序(metagenomic next-generation sequencing，mNGS)结果为鉴定出40个属于肺炎链球菌基因组的特定序列和25个属于脓肿分枝杆菌基因组的特定序列，同时，该BALF标本常规微生物学检查结果示细菌、真菌培养均为阴性。考虑到头孢他啶可覆盖肺炎链球菌，且当前脓肿分枝杆菌感染诊断依据不足，继续予以头孢他啶抗感染治疗。 患儿2023年7月29日胸片(A)与2023年10月24日胸片(B)对比 Figure 1 Comparison of chest X-rays of the pediatric patient taken on July 29, 2023 (A) and October 24, 2023 (B) A: On July 29, 2023, the chest X-ray showing patchy high-density shadows in both lung fields with poor boundary, which was considered to be an infection of both lungs.

pmc-13476681.title: Beyond VDR: Vitamin D Metabolism Genes in Tuberculosis Susceptibility, Immune Response and Implications for Diabetes Mellitus
pmc-13476681.creator: Marrita Rabadi, Zaeem Hussain, Sundus Farooq Siddiqui, Hiba Farooq Siddiqui, Michail Nomikos, Mohammed Seed Ahmed
pmc-13476681.description: BackgroundVitamin D is an important immunomodulator in host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, yet most tuberculosis-related research has focused on the vitamin D receptor (VDR). The contribution of vitamin D metabolism genes, particularly cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes, remains less clearly defined.

pmc-13614979.title: Modulating auditory attention and stimulus evaluation in the medial prefrontal cortex: A translational tone approach oddball paradigm in rats
pmc-13614979.creator: Marcel R. Oelerich, Yannis Pfleger, Mesbah Alam, Joachim K. Krauss, Kerstin Schwabe, Franziska M. Decker
pmc-13614979.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The three-class auditory oddball paradigm is used to study sensory processing, attention, and decision-making. In this paradigm, a rare behaviorally relevant target is presented among frequent behaviorally irrelevant standard and rare distractor tones. The Tone Approach Paradigm (TAP) was designed as a variation of this paradigm in which task difficulty increases as the target and distractor frequencies sequentially approach the frequency of the standard tone to investigate neurocognitive aspects of processing behaviorally relevant auditory stimuli under challenging hearing conditions in rats.
